# General Rules

- **Any form of cheating in runs will result in you being banned from the leaderboards.**
- All runs done on 1.13 (Aquatic) and under are to be submitted to Standard Trading System
- PS4/PS5 are to be submitted to New Trading System unless played on Older Versions.
- Emulators are allowed.
- You are to play on any publicly released Title Update of the game. This excludes any Beta or Dev Builds.
- Different variations of a console must be submitted under the main console (Xbox One S to Xbox One)
- Any% Glitched runs played on versions before TU46 are to be submitted to the "Pre TU46" category.
- Demos are allowed but restricted to only tutorial world categories.
- Certain In-Game Exploits including:
    - Text Box Exploit
    - Save Exploit
    - Trade Exploit

-***Reset Dimension is only allowed in Glitched Runs***

- Creative Mode Glitch (CMG) is banned
- Peaceful Mode isn't allowed for runs
- ***Please refrain from submitting Bedrock runs as there is a separate leaderboard for said game***
___
#Timing Rules
- All categories now use the RTA w Set Loads Timing format which removes all Dimension Loads, and replaces these specific loading screens with this format:
    - **Closing and Opening the game | 30 seconds**
    - **Relogging in the world              | 10 seconds**
    - **Saving the game                       | 04 seconds**
    - **(Disabling/Enabling Autosave)  | 04 seconds**

- Timing starts upon first player input, this includes the following:
    - Movement (Walking or looking around)
    - Opening the Crafting Interface, Inventory, or the Player-Select Screen   
- Tutorial World runs start upon first player input or accepting or declining the Basics Tutorial text box prompt
- Timing ends depending on the category (All Any% Runs end upon the first frame of the End-Poem displaying on-screen)
- Pausing the game, changing your perspective, or opening the game settings does not count as first player input
- You are given a Grace Period before timing starts (about 1:30)
- If you leave the world, open the HOME menu or quit the game for anything, the timer must stay running
- You cannot pause the timer by any means

___

# Coop Rules

- Timing starts when all players involved in the run joins the game. (First frame of the "player has joined the game." message or in the Player Interface from the Select Button.)
- Other players **MUST** contribute to the run in some way such as gathering resources or helping the host with the route they're following. Failure to do so will result in the run being rejected.
- If the Host moves, opens their inventory, or Crafting Interface, timing will start. This also applies to joining players
- Only one player has to enter the Exit Portal, preferably the Host shows their POV as they enter
- Splitscreen Coop is allowed
- If a run is done by one person with two controllers, the second controller has to contribute to the run in some way and must be submitted to Coop (Ex: Alt Duping).
- If a player leaves and never joins back, the run will be rejected as all players must be in the game for the run to count
- If a player is not part of the run, joins the world, and interferes, the run will be invalid. Make sure you set your game to "Invite Only" 
    - *Any% Tutorial World Coop runs played Online will now require that you show you creating a new save of the tutorial world, Save and Exiting the world, then enabling online for every attempt. Moving from the spawn during this will result in your run being rejected. All Coop Rules still apply.*

___

# Video Proof Rules

- *All submissions require video proof that is viewable*
- Any form of media is acceptable, but YouTube videos and Twitch Vods are highly suggested.
- YT videos must be either *Public or Unlisted*
- A YouTube video MUST remain either Unlisted or Public. The same applies for highlighting Twitch Vods.
- Minimal video quality we'll accept is 480p 30FPS (any videos under 30FPS and 480p may be accepted, but it is encouraged to have the accepted video quality.)
- Any recording method is acceptable as long as we can view the video
- If the video has too many cuts, speedups, or slowdowns, the run will be either verified or rejected. Mainly depends if it is watchable
- The video CANNOT be tampered with to gain an unfair advantage. Examples include:
    - Splicing
    - Changing the speed of the video
- Some legal edits that can be used include: 
    - Adding Music
    - Adding text
    - Adding intros
    - Adding post commentary
- Any use of these edits to disguise cheating is strictly prohibited and will result in your run being rejected.
- Troll Submissions are obviously not allowed. You will be banned from the site for *Spam* if you do this!
- Audio is not required for submission but is recommended that you do so
- If a submission is a Livestream or a video with many attempts, please specify the part of the run with a timestamp

___

# Emulator Rules

- Currently, only RPCS3, Xenia, Cemu, Yuzu, and WinDurango. You can find the links on how to set them up in the Guides tab
- Runs done on Emulator MUST be capped to the original game's framerate (60FPS)
- FPS must be shown on screen to ensure the run is capped, if you can't do this for whatever reason, show your Framerate Settings after the run is over. 
- You may use external FPS Displays to prove the game's framerate.
- Uncapped runs will be rejected
- Any use of external tools or settings in these emulators are strictly prohibited and will result in an automatic rejection, these include:
    - Slowdown
    - Savestates


# Xenia Rules

- Runs done on Xenia MUST be played on the latest builds of Xenia Master and Canary. Any previously submitted runs done on older builds that are under TU12 will remain untouched.
- You are free to use either DirectX12 or Vulkan to play the game.
- To show framerate, either install an FPS display or send the Xenia .config file.

# Modding Rules

- Mods that are acceptable include:
    - Custom Skins (Recommended not to use giant skins or ones that cover most of the screen)
    - Custom Capes
    - Custom Music
    - Custom UI
    - Texture Packs that don't provide an advantage
    - Modding your game to go back to an certain version of the game (
- Mods that are ***NOT*** acceptable include:
    - Full Bright
    - Texture Packs that provide a clear advantage like Highlighted Important Blocks and X-Ray
    - Changing Game Files to gain an unfair advantage
**(NOTE: When using modded textures from somewhere else or using a personal one, it's best to show the moderators so we can verify if it will be allowed or not. In-Game Texture Packs are allowed.)**

Among Us originally released in 2018 but has seen a huge surge in popularity over the past couple of week**s. This had led many new __players to pick up Innersloth’s little party game and has spurred a ton of new questions about the game, the genre it fits into, and even what exactly the point of Among Us is. Thankfully, we’ve already put in a solid number of hours, which means we can help you understand everything there is to know, including how to play Among UsHow to play Among UsHow to play Among Us - dead bodyPlaying Among Us might seem difficult at first, but the basic premise of the game is extremely simple. Basically, there are two types of players: Crewmate and Impostors. You can have anywhere from 1-3 Impostors in your game, which ups the stakes at play exponentially.The biggest difference between Among Us and other games in this genre, though, is the fact that you aren’t allowed to talk during the main game phase. After dead bodies are reported, or when an Emergency Meeting is called, you’ll be able to discuss who the Impostor is. Otherwise, though, the game builds up tension and anxiety by forcing players to remain silent as they complete their tasks.More Among Us GuidesGuide Name	DescriptionHow to play Impostor	Everything you need to know to get better at playing Impostor inAmong Us.How to play as a Crewmate	Learn the basics of playing a Crewmate in Among Us.How to close doors	Want to know how to close doors in Among Us? We can help.How to get pets	Learn how to get pets and spice up your life in Among Us.How to use vents	Find out how use vents in Among Us.How to change keyboard controlsTired of moving around with your mouse? Learn how to change over to keyboard controls.How to use the character creatorFind out more about the character creation system in Among Us.How to play as a CrewmateHow to play Among Us as CrewmateCrewmates will spend the majority of the game trying to figure out who the Impostor is while also completing a series of tasks. As a member of the crew, your goal is to either complete all of the tasks or to figure out who the Impostor (or Impostors) are and then expel them from the game. Make sure to report any dead bodies that you find, and try to look out for anyone being suspicious about the body. If you find yourself killed by the Impostor, you can still complete tasks to help your fellow Crewmates win.As a Crewmate, try to look out for any weird actions from other players. If anyone seems like they are trying to stick to the shadows or just stay out of sight. You’ll also want to pay careful attention to players as they complete tasks. Some of the tasks actually have animations associated with them, which you can sometimes use to tell if someone is lying about doing the task. When you’ve gathered enough evidence – or have an idea of who the Impostor is, bring it up during the Discussion phase and try to make your case.How to play as an ImpostorHow to play Among Us as the ImpostorThose playing the Impostor will need to pretend to complete various tasks around the map while also taking out the Crewmates. If you’re playing with multiple Impostors, then you can work together to take out the crew much quicker, allowing you to secure your win. Impostors have access to a Sabotage menu that they can use to overheat the reactor, turn off the lights, or even mess with the base’s oxygen levels. Impostors can also use Vents to get around the map much quicker. Keep in mind that any crewmate that sees you will know that you’re the Impostor and can call an Emergency Meeting to vote you out.Obviously, as an Impostor, try to familiarize yourself with the various tasks so that any alibis you provide seem plausible. You will also want to avoid outright accusing anyone else or pushing too hard on someone’s accusation, as this can often be seen as you trying to get a Crewmate ejected. It’s fine to agree with others, but don’t go so hard on the accusation that you bring attention to yourself instead. Being a great Impostor takes practice and skill, and also the ability to lie really well. For more tips and info on how to play Impostor, please take a look at our handy guide.That’s a basic breakdown of how to play Among Us. The game is available on PC and mobile devices, so make sure you pick it up and give it a try if you’re looking for a fun party game to dive into with your friends.

Set Seed Rules

Random Seed Rules
You are required to use a random seed
The seed input box must be left completely blank
You may not learn the seed during the run
Do not do /seed

JP 1.0 VC inject is not allowed

Auto-rejection:
We use a bot to auto-reject runs which do not fill out the submission forms correctly. To avoid auto rejection be sure to do the following:
Do not change the "verified" option (leave it as "Yes", this is for our use only)
Do not include milliseconds, these are only for top level runs, the milliseconds on your livesplit timer are irrelevant and inaccurate
If on emulator be sure to select EMU as subcategory AND check the emulator box for platform

Entire run in one segment
Must include audible game audio
Twitch VODs must be highlighted

For N64/EMU, the first frame of the Super Mario 64 logo should appear at 1.33 seconds.
For Wii/Wii U VC timing starts on reset (the first frame the screen goes black before the classic controller text/mario logo) and ends when the big star is collected at the end of the game.

The re-mapping scheme at the beginning of the run must remain for the entirety of the run. games.name: Minecraft: Legacy Console Edition
games.rules:
# General Rules

- **Any form of cheating in runs will result in you being banned from the leaderboards.**
- All runs done on 1.13 (Aquatic) and under are to be submitted to Standard Trading System
- PS4/PS5 are to be submitted to New Trading System unless played on Older Versions.
- Emulators are allowed.
- You are to play on any publicly released Title Update of the game. This excludes any Beta or Dev Builds.
- Different variations of a console must be submitted under the main console (Xbox One S to Xbox One)
- Any% Glitched runs played on versions before TU46 are to be submitted to the "Pre TU46" category.
- Demos are allowed but restricted to only tutorial world categories.
- Certain In-Game Exploits including:
    - Text Box Exploit
    - Save Exploit
    - Trade Exploit

-***Reset Dimension is only allowed in Glitched Runs***

- Creative Mode Glitch (CMG) is banned
- Peaceful Mode isn't allowed for runs
- ***Please refrain from submitting Bedrock runs as there is a separate leaderboard for said game***
___
#Timing Rules
- All categories now use the RTA w Set Loads Timing format which removes all Dimension Loads, and replaces these specific loading screens with this format:
    - **Closing and Opening the game | 30 seconds**
    - **Relogging in the world              | 10 seconds**
    - **Saving the game                       | 04 seconds**
    - **(Disabling/Enabling Autosave)  | 04 seconds**

- Timing starts upon first player input, this includes the following:
    - Movement (Walking or looking around)
    - Opening the Crafting Interface, Inventory, or the Player-Select Screen   
- Tutorial World runs start upon first player input or accepting or declining the Basics Tutorial text box prompt
- Timing ends depending on the category (All Any% Runs end upon the first frame of the End-Poem displaying on-screen)
- Pausing the game, changing your perspective, or opening the game settings does not count as first player input
- You are given a Grace Period before timing starts (about 1:30)
- If you leave the world, open the HOME menu or quit the game for anything, the timer must stay running
- You cannot pause the timer by any means

___

# Coop Rules

- Timing starts when all players involved in the run joins the game. (First frame of the "player has joined the game." message or in the Player Interface from the Select Button.)
- Other players **MUST** contribute to the run in some way such as gathering resources or helping the host with the route they're following. Failure to do so will result in the run being rejected.
- If the Host moves, opens their inventory, or Crafting Interface, timing will start. This also applies to joining players
- Only one player has to enter the Exit Portal, preferably the Host shows their POV as they enter
- Splitscreen Coop is allowed
- If a run is done by one person with two controllers, the second controller has to contribute to the run in some way and must be submitted to Coop (Ex: Alt Duping).
- If a player leaves and never joins back, the run will be rejected as all players must be in the game for the run to count
- If a player is not part of the run, joins the world, and interferes, the run will be invalid. Make sure you set your game to "Invite Only" 
    - *Any% Tutorial World Coop runs played Online will now require that you show you creating a new save of the tutorial world, Save and Exiting the world, then enabling online for every attempt. Moving from the spawn during this will result in your run being rejected. All Coop Rules still apply.*

___

# Video Proof Rules

- *All submissions require video proof that is viewable*
- Any form of media is acceptable, but YouTube videos and Twitch Vods are highly suggested.
- YT videos must be either *Public or Unlisted*
- A YouTube video MUST remain either Unlisted or Public. The same applies for highlighting Twitch Vods.
- Minimal video quality we'll accept is 480p 30FPS (any videos under 30FPS and 480p may be accepted, but it is encouraged to have the accepted video quality.)
- Any recording method is acceptable as long as we can view the video
- If the video has too many cuts, speedups, or slowdowns, the run will be either verified or rejected. Mainly depends if it is watchable
- The video CANNOT be tampered with to gain an unfair advantage. Examples include:
    - Splicing
    - Changing the speed of the video
- Some legal edits that can be used include: 
    - Adding Music
    - Adding text
    - Adding intros
    - Adding post commentary
- Any use of these edits to disguise cheating is strictly prohibited and will result in your run being rejected.
- Troll Submissions are obviously not allowed. You will be banned from the site for *Spam* if you do this!
- Audio is not required for submission but is recommended that you do so
- If a submission is a Livestream or a video with many attempts, please specify the part of the run with a timestamp

___

# Emulator Rules

- Currently, only RPCS3, Xenia, Cemu, Yuzu, and WinDurango. You can find the links on how to set them up in the Guides tab
- Runs done on Emulator MUST be capped to the original game's framerate (60FPS)
- FPS must be shown on screen to ensure the run is capped, if you can't do this for whatever reason, show your Framerate Settings after the run is over. 
- You may use external FPS Displays to prove the game's framerate.
- Uncapped runs will be rejected
- Any use of external tools or settings in these emulators are strictly prohibited and will result in an automatic rejection, these include:
    - Slowdown
    - Savestates


# Xenia Rules

- Runs done on Xenia MUST be played on the latest builds of Xenia Master and Canary. Any previously submitted runs done on older builds that are under TU12 will remain untouched.
- You are free to use either DirectX12 or Vulkan to play the game.
- To show framerate, either install an FPS display or send the Xenia .config file.

# Modding Rules

- Mods that are acceptable include:
    - Custom Skins (Recommended not to use giant skins or ones that cover most of the screen)
    - Custom Capes
    - Custom Music
    - Custom UI
    - Texture Packs that don't provide an advantage
    - Modding your game to go back to an certain version of the game (
- Mods that are ***NOT*** acceptable include:
    - Full Bright
    - Texture Packs that provide a clear advantage like Highlighted Important Blocks and X-Ray
    - Changing Game Files to gain an unfair advantage
**(NOTE: When using modded textures from somewhere else or using a personal one, it's best to show the moderators so we can verify if it will be allowed or not. In-Game Texture Packs are allowed.)**
